states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Cyprus: its kings are subjects of the Persian king; its waters carry Cyrus' fleet past to Issus

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Phoenicia: the King's general Abrocomas gathers an army here, then falls back before Cyrus

states.name: Syria
timeline: Myriandus, the Chalus, Thapsacus: Cyrus names his real target and the army fords the Euphrates

states.name: Georgia
timeline: Colchis: the 'Colchians' the Greeks fought above Trapezus lived west of today's Georgia

states.name: Azerbaijan
timeline: Beyond the route, in the King's northern satrapies

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Cyrus' army marches from Sardis over the Taurus to Tarsus; by December the retreating Greeks are fighting through the Carduchian mountains into Armenia
Through the Armenian snows to Mount Theches and Trapezus, then along the Black Sea coast to Byzantium
The survivors are handed over to the Spartan Thibron for war on the Persian satraps
King Agesilaus of Sparta campaigns in Asia Minor, with Xenophon at his side
Agesilaus is recalled to fight in Greece

states.name: Armenia
timeline: East of the route: ancient Armenia reached far into today's eastern Turkey, where the army wintered

states.name: Greece
timeline: Xenophon's Athens, beaten by Sparta in 404, under a restored democracy
Athens tries and executes Socrates, Xenophon's teacher
Coronea: Xenophon fights beside Agesilaus against a coalition that includes Athens

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Cunaxa: Cyrus is killed; the generals are seized at the Zapatas; the Greeks fight their way up the Tigris

states.name: Iran
timeline: The King's heartland: Susa, Ecbatana and Persepolis, which the Greeks never reached

states.name: Bulgaria
timeline: Thrace: the lands of the Odrysian kings
Winter 400/399: the army serves the Thracian prince Seuthes, who cheats it of its pay

events.title: Cyrus musters
events.text: In the spring Cyrus leaves Sardis, saying he is marching against the Pisidian hill tribes.

events.title: Review at Celaenae
events.text: After thirty days at Celaenae, Cyrus counts 11,000 hoplites and about 2,000 peltasts.

events.title: A mock charge
events.text: Reviewing the army for Queen Epyaxa of Cilicia, the Greeks charge in jest and the market people flee.

events.title: Mutiny at Tarsus
events.text: The soldiers suspect they are marching against the King and refuse to go on; Clearchus talks them round.

events.title: Ships at Issus
events.text: Cyrus' fleet arrives; the Spartan Chirisophus brings 700 hoplites.

events.title: Two generals desert
events.text: Xenias and Pasion slip away by ship from Myriandus; Cyrus lets them go.

events.title: Thapsacus
events.text: Cyrus admits his target, his brother the King, and the army fords the Euphrates.

events.title: Through the desert
events.text: Marching down the Euphrates through 'Arabia', the army sees wild asses and ostriches; pack animals starve.

events.title: Orontas condemned
events.text: A Persian noble caught betraying Cyrus is tried in his tent and never seen again.

events.title: Battle of Cunaxa
events.text: The Greeks rout the wing before them, but Cyrus is killed charging his brother.

events.title: Weapons demanded
events.text: The King orders the Greeks to surrender their arms; they refuse.

events.title: Across the Tigris
events.text: Under a truce with Tissaphernes, the Greeks cross the Tigris on a bridge of boats.

events.title: The generals seized
events.text: At the Zapatas, Tissaphernes seizes five generals at a conference; they are beheaded.

events.title: Xenophon elected
events.text: Xenophon, who held no command, rallies the officers and is elected in place of Proxenus.

events.title: Slingers and horsemen
events.text: Xenophon raises 200 Rhodian slingers and 50 horsemen to keep the Persians at a distance.

events.title: Larisa and Mespila
events.text: The army passes the ruins of two great cities, today's Nimrud and Nineveh.

events.title: The hollow square
events.text: Six reserve companies of 100 men fix the hollow square's trouble at bridges and passes.

events.title: Into the mountains
events.text: The King's army stops; for seven days the Carduchians attack from the heights.

events.title: The Kentrites
events.text: Under attack from both banks, the Greeks force a crossing into Armenia.

events.title: Tiribazus' camp
events.text: The satrap of western Armenia plans an ambush; the Greeks strike his camp first.

events.title: Snow a fathom deep
events.text: The north wind freezes men where they stand; many lose toes or their sight.

events.title: Underground villages
events.text: The army winters in Armenian houses dug into the earth and drinks barley beer through straws.

events.title: The Taochian fortress
events.text: When the Greeks storm a stronghold, its women throw their children and themselves off the cliff.

events.title: Thalatta! Thalatta!
events.text: From Mount Theches the vanguard sees the Black Sea; the soldiers build a great cairn.

events.title: The Colchians
events.text: The army attacks a Colchian line on a mountain in columns of companies; then wild honey drugs many soldiers.

events.title: Trapezus
events.text: At the Greek city of Trapezus the army sacrifices and holds games on a steep hillside.

events.title: The count at Cerasus
events.text: The generals review the army: 8,600 men under arms survive.

events.title: Cotyora
events.text: Forty-five days; Xenophon dreams of founding a city, and answers charges of striking his men.

events.title: Sinope
events.text: The army sails to Sinope and elects the Spartan Chirisophus sole commander, for a week.

events.title: The army splits
events.text: At Heraclea the Arcadians and Achaeans break away; the army divides in three.

events.title: Calpe Harbour
events.text: The divided army reunites after heavy losses and beats Pharnabazus' cavalry.

events.title: Byzantium
events.text: Shut out of the city, the soldiers break in; Xenophon persuades them not to sack it.

events.title: Sold as slaves
events.text: The Spartan governor Aristarchus sells some 400 soldiers left in Byzantium into slavery.

events.title: Seuthes
events.text: Through the winter the army raids Thracian villages for the prince Seuthes, who withholds its pay.

events.title: Socrates executed
events.text: In Athens, Xenophon's teacher Socrates is tried for impiety and put to death.

events.title: Handed to Thibron
events.text: At Pergamum the survivors join the Spartan Thibron's war on the Persian satraps.

events.title: Agesilaus in Asia
events.text: King Agesilaus of Sparta lands at Ephesus to free the Greek cities from Persia.

events.title: Victory near Sardis
events.text: Agesilaus beats Tissaphernes' cavalry by the river Pactolus.

events.title: Tissaphernes executed
events.text: At Colossae, with Cyrus' old ally Ariaeus helping, the King's men seize and behead Tissaphernes.

events.title: Cnidus
events.text: A Persian fleet under the Athenian Conon destroys Sparta's navy.

events.title: Battle of Coronea
events.text: Agesilaus, with Xenophon beside him, defeats the Thebans and their allies, Athens among them.

eras: With Sparta in Asia and Greece
chartNote: Share of the area of eleven modern countries, by what the march meant there each year. Regions are today's boundaries, and a whole country takes one colour: most of the route, from Sardis to the Armenian snows and the Black Sea coast, lies in today's Turkey. The film's route map shows the march stage by stage.
